localBiteReport: The most recent available report covering Choctawhatchee Bay is from the week of September 4–10, 2026 — roughly 10 days old, not this week. According to Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters (via Great Days Outdoors), the bay is showing the first signs of the fall transition, with large schools of baitfish pushing from deeper open water onto flats, bayous, and bridge areas. Sight-fishing opportunities for redfish on the flats are described as improving, and the prior week's report (Aug 28–Sept 3) noted that the arrival of slot reds in earnest is expected during the second or third week of September as the mullet run gets underway — which puts us right at that window now with water temps at 87°F. Trout, flounder, sheepshead, and black drum were not called out specifically in these reports, but fall transitions in the bay historically activate all of those species as bait schools compress and water temps begin to ease.
